title: Noble Sissle's secret: swing without noise
summary: Briggs says Sissle's secret for high society was to play as you like but not noisily, a principle Briggs adopted.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yes, but not too loud, as I told you.

And that was Noble Sissle's secret. Noble Sissle's secret was that he had -- he played for the high society, as you say. And his secret was, you can play as you want to, but not noisy. You can give them what you want, but not boisterously, you see. And that's -- well I kept that not only as a motto, I kept that idea which was musical, very musical. You can swing and bounce as much as you want to. You don't have to blow the house down, you know, in order to swing, you don't have to.
You don't have to, you understand, --
Fight your instrument. You don't have to fight your instrument to swing, you see.
And we -- that type of music, we played at that time, you can play as you want to, but don't annoy the patron.
